chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Coltsville Harris, Jesse Price and Paul Barbarin
summary: DeMichael asks about Armstrong's big-band drummer; Saunders contrasts Paul Barbarin's New Orleans flavor with Catlett.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: Freed it up a little bit. You mentioned Sid Catlett. Oh, yes, did you ever hear a drummer named Coltsville Harris?
I heard --
Worked with Louis.
Yeah, I heard thename, but I never, never met him.
He's one of my boyhood heroes.
Oh, no kidding?
Used to hear Louis' big band when I was in Louisville.
Right, right.
And he was a drummer.
Uh-huh.
Very much like Sid Catlett. He'd get that dark sound.
Right, right, right, right.
And -- but very few people have heard of him.
Right, I --
He used to wear this big white towel around his --
I heard of him. Back there there was some real -- Jesse Price was another out of Kansas City. I don't know whether you ever heard of him or not.
Oh, yes, on records.
Oh, oh, yeah, right. Jesse was a real nice guy, and then Louis -- I mean, with Louis, when he was with Lu Russell's band, they had Paul Barbarin.
Right, he was from New Orleans.
Right, New Orleans type drummer. So this is what I was talking, when I was saying about different flavors. And it was a different flavor all together with that band than with Big Sid Catlett.
